question: A food bank's pantry held 161 canned goods at the start of the month. A donation drive added 26 more cans. A large distribution then gave away 117 cans to local families. A grocery store then donated 24 more cans, and a school food drive added 53 more. Volunteers spent about 60 minutes sorting the shelves, which they logged as exactly 1 hour. Finally, 61 cans were sent to a neighboring pantry in need. How many canned goods remained in the pantry?

A toy drive started with 94 boxes of donated toys at a collection center. A citywide push left the center with 9 times as many boxes. A large shipment of 723 boxes was sent to a downtown shelter. A separate delivery of 49 boxes went to a rural shelter. A last-minute donation then doubled the remaining boxes. A volunteer coordinator also mentioned there were about 15 vans available that day, though that number played no role in the toy count. Finally, 71 more boxes arrived from a corporate sponsor. How many boxes of toys were at the collection center in the end?

Two roommates, Jordan and Kim, split grocery costs, but this story follows only Jordan's running total, which began at 116 dollars, more than Kim owed that month. In the morning, Jordan added 54 dollars after a supply run. In the afternoon, a refund added 14 more dollars to his total. That evening, a matching reimbursement from his employer left him with 4 times as much. The paperwork for that reimbursement took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour, to process. Finally, that total was split evenly 2 ways between Jordan and a joint account he shares with his brother, leaving just Jordan's share. How much money did Jordan's share come to in the end?

Two cousins, Ana and Beto, collect seashells, but this story follows only Ana's collection, which started at 40 shells that morning, well ahead of Beto's count. In the morning, a beach trip left her with 3 times as many shells. In the afternoon, a swap meet with other collectors multiplied her shells by 9. That evening, a friend gave her 8 more shells found near the pier. A local shop was selling shell necklaces for 22 dollars each, unrelated to her count. Finally, a matching gift from her grandmother doubled her shells once more. How many shells did Ana end up with by the end of the evening?

A charity raffle sold 205 tickets by the morning. By late morning, 23 more tickets were sold at a school booth, and at noon the tickets were split evenly across 4 volunteer boxes, this story following just one box. In the afternoon, that box received 11 more tickets from a walk-up table, and a radio station then multiplied its count by 7 for a bonus drawing that took about 120 minutes, right around 2 hours. That evening, a matching sponsor multiplied the total by 9 for the grand prize pool. A volunteer mentioned handing out a dozen pencils that day, unrelated to the ticket count. How many tickets were in the grand prize pool by the end of the evening?

A bakery had 176 loaves of bread ready at sunrise. In the morning, a catering order left the bakery needing 5 times as many loaves. In the afternoon, 365 loaves were sold to walk-in customers. Later that afternoon, an extra batch added 76 more loaves. That evening, a wholesale client multiplied the remaining loaves by 7 for a citywide order. A sign out front advertised a dozen cupcakes for 9 dollars, unrelated to the bread count. How many loaves of bread did the bakery have by the end of the evening?

A single warehouse pallet started the morning with 208 sealed boxes. In the morning, 58 boxes were pulled for a damaged inspection. By midday, a matching shipment left the pallet with 6 times as many boxes. In the afternoon, a regional distributor multiplied that count by 7, and a second matching distributor multiplied it by 7 again. That evening, 34 more boxes were added from a late truck. A worker mentioned there were about a dozen forklifts in the yard, unrelated to this pallet's count. Finally, a closing bulk order multiplied the pallet's boxes by 6 once more. How many boxes were on this one pallet by the end of the evening?

A food truck started the morning with 94 tacos prepped. A breakfast rush left the truck needing 7 times as many tacos. In the afternoon, the crew prepped 53 more tacos, and a catering order added 16 more. A large event then used up 116 tacos. That evening, a second location matched the remaining count 3 times over, and a third location matched it 4 times over. Prep for the evening rush took about 90 minutes, roughly an hour and a half. How many tacos were ready across the locations by the end of the evening?

Two food trucks, Rosa's and Kenji's, split a produce order, but this story follows only Rosa's crates, which started at 130 total, more than Kenji usually orders. The order was divided evenly among 5 trucks in her fleet, following just one truck, whose crates were then matched 9 times over for a festival contract. Those festival crates were split evenly among 3 vendor stalls, following just one stall, which received 40 more crates from a late supplier. A citywide inspection then multiplied that stall's crates by 5. A nearby stall was fined 75 dollars for a permit issue, unrelated to Rosa's count. Finally, the stall's crates were split evenly one more time among 5 shelves. How many crates ended up on one shelf?

A single food pantry shelf started the day with 73 cans of soup. Volunteers distributed 45 cans to families that morning. A donation drive then left the shelf with 3 times as many cans. A grocery store added 44 more cans in the afternoon, but 52 cans were given out to a shelter that evening. A coordinator mentioned a dozen volunteers helped that day, though their number played no role in the can count. Finally, a matching grant multiplied the shelf's cans by 5. How many cans were on that one shelf in the end?

A food stand had 38 hot dogs ready at sunrise. In the morning, 74 more hot dogs were grilled for the breakfast crowd. In the afternoon, 54 hot dogs were sold at lunch rush. Later that afternoon, a catering order left the remaining stock 3 times as large. That evening, 16 more hot dogs were grilled for a late event, but 119 were then sold to a large group. How many hot dogs did the stand have by the end of the evening?

A single grain elevator started the day with 163 bushels of corn. A local co-op delivery left the elevator with 3 times as much corn. A regional contract then multiplied that amount by 7. A rail shipment of 3283 bushels was sent out to a mill. A final harvest bonus multiplied the remaining corn by 9. The rail shipment took about 300 minutes to load, right around 5 hours. How many bushels of corn were left in the elevator?

Two vineyard owners, Marco and Elise, track their grape crates, but this story follows only Marco's crates, which started at 87, fewer than Elise's harvest. A bumper season left Marco with 9 times as many crates. He then received 66 more crates from a neighboring field, and 31 more from a late pick. A wholesale buyer took 318 crates, after a pickup that took about 120 minutes, right around 2 hours. A second buyer then took 304 more crates. How many crates did Marco have left?

A single food pantry started the day with 178 pounds of rice. A donation added 45 more pounds that morning. A matching grant then doubled the pantry's total. A large family event used 437 pounds over the weekend. A grocery store then donated 42 more pounds, after a delivery that took about 30 minutes, roughly half an hour. Finally, 13 more pounds arrived from a community garden. How many pounds of rice did the pantry have in the end?

A charity auction raised 207 dollars by sunrise. In the morning, a surprise bidder added 74 more dollars. By midday, a matching sponsor multiplied the total by 9. In the afternoon, a second matching sponsor multiplied it by 5 once more. That evening, the total was split evenly among 3 partner charities, and this story follows just one charity's share. A volunteer mentioned a dozen raffle baskets were given away, unrelated to the money count. How much money did that one charity receive in the end?

A single delivery truck started the morning with 104 crates of soda loaded. A stop at the first store removed 60 crates. The remaining crates were then split evenly between 2 routes, and this story follows just one route. A regional distributor then multiplied that route's crates by 7. Finally, 75 more crates were added from a warehouse stop, after a drive that took about 40 minutes, just under 1 hour. How many crates were on that route by the end?

A single fish tank started the morning with 62 guppies. By midmorning, a breeding boom left the tank with 8 times as many guppies. In the afternoon, a matching tank multiplied that count by 5. Later that afternoon, 30 more guppies were added from a pet shop trade. A nearby tank held 15 goldfish, unrelated to this tank's count. That evening, a final breeding cycle multiplied the tank's guppies by 6. How many guppies were in that one tank by the end of the evening?

Two shop owners, Yusuf and Delia, track inventory, but this story follows only Yusuf's stock of phone cases, which started at 91, fewer than Delia's stock. A bulk order left Yusuf with 8 times as many cases. A wholesale buyer then took 597 cases off his hands. A new shipment added 72 more cases. A supplier catalog also listed a case model for 25 dollars, unrelated to Yusuf's count. Finally, a holiday order multiplied his remaining cases by 9. How many phone cases did Yusuf have in the end?

Two siblings, Owen and Mia, save coins in separate piggy banks, but this story follows only Owen's bank, which started at 139 coins, more than Mia's bank held. He added 51 more coins from his allowance. A matching gift from his grandfather then multiplied his coins by 9. A birthday added 58 more coins to his bank. Finally, he split his coins evenly between 2 new jars, and this story follows just one jar. How many coins were in that one jar in the end?

A warehouse had 224 pallets of canned vegetables at the start of the day. A retailer order removed 156 pallets that morning, and a supplier delivered 18 more pallets that afternoon. A quality check then pulled 37 pallets for inspection, while a second supplier added 77 more. A citywide distributor then left the warehouse with 3 times as many pallets. Finally, 15 more pallets arrived from a delayed truck, around the time gas prices hit 4 dollars a gallon, unrelated to the pallet count. How many pallets did the warehouse have in the end?

A single food bank warehouse started the week with 211 crates of vegetables. A matching donation drive left it with 6 times as many crates. A large distribution then used up 1120 crates for local shelters. A regional partner multiplied the remaining crates by 5. A grocery chain then added 66 more crates, after a delivery that took about 90 minutes, roughly an hour and a half. Finally, a matching year-end donation doubled the warehouse's crates. How many crates were in the warehouse in the end?

A single comic book collection started with 118 issues in a long box. A convention haul left the box with 4 times as many issues. A trade-in booth then removed 35 issues that didn't sell. A matching set from a dealer tripled the remaining issues. A second matching set multiplied the count by 3 again. Finally, 2123 issues were donated to a library sale. How many comic books were left in the collection?

A single beehive started spring with 28 worker bees in a starter colony. A strong nectar season left the hive with 8 times as many bees. A second growth spurt multiplied the colony by 4. A third growth spurt then multiplied it by 6. Finally, a swarm merger added 48 more bees. A neighboring hive was said to hold about 900 bees, a separate count from this one. How many bees were in this hive in the end?

Two collectors, Priya and Owen, save vintage coins, but this story follows only Priya's collection, which started at 238 coins, more than Owen owned. She added 22 more coins from an estate sale, and 14 more from a swap meet. A dealer's matching offer then left her with 8 times as many coins. A museum trade multiplied her collection by 9. A final auction multiplied it by 3 once more, after a bidding session that lasted about 120 minutes, right around 2 hours. How many coins did Priya have in the end?

A single garden plot started spring with 17 tomato seedlings. A neighbor gave 33 more seedlings that week. A nursery donated 7 more seedlings the next week. A community swap then left the plot with 6 times as many seedlings. Finally, 58 more seedlings arrived from a school program. A separate plot down the street grew about a dozen pumpkins, unrelated to the tomato count. How many tomato seedlings were in that plot in the end?
